newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European equities stride into record books.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European equities stride into record books.

text.p: European share markets rose strongly on Monday, with at least six bourses striding into record territory as Wall Street continued its rally and Tokyo staged a rebound.

French, Swiss, Swedish, Spanish and Belgian stock indices closed at record highs. Frankfurt posted a trading record and Dutch stocks came within a whisker of setting a record too. Tokyo shares leapt 4.75 percent following savage losses last week, while London's FTSE 100 index regained the 4,100 level as fears receded of an imminent rise in British interest rates.
Wall Street followed through on Friday's record close by rising further in morning trade. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up around 10 points as European markets closed.

On foreign exchange markets, the dollar closed just off two year highs against the mark, the Swiss franc and the French franc as dealers braced themselves for further evidence of buoyant economic growth in the U.S.

Wall Street's Friday record provided the major early impetus to European stocks, giving the Paris bourse the shove required for it join London and Frankfurt in the record books where they have been for months.

France's CAC-40 index hit a closing high of 2,361.27 points, surpassing the previous high of 2,355.93 set on February 2, 1994 and underlining the recent strength of the French market, which had lagged its main European rivals.
The blue chip index rose 1.4 percent in a rally fuelled by Wall Street's rise and expectations of higher French corporate earnings this year.

"The fundamentals are good for the bourse, and they haven't changed -- interest rates are low, corporate profits are expected to rise on moderate economic growth, productivity is improving, and exchange rates are favourable with the franc's decline against the Italian lira, British sterling and dollar," said George de Nesmeskery Kiss, economist at Societe Generale.

Carmaker Renault, which has languished for weeks, showed the biggest gain with a rise of 4.15 percent to 113 francs after chairman Louis Schweitzer said he hoped the company's car operation's would break even this year.
German shares also opened bourse trade at a record high of 2,961.25. The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 21.56 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,954.95 but off its trading high of 2,961.25.
"I think the 3,000 points is still on, but I would prefer it after a consolidation down to around 2,880 first," one dealer said.
British shares also closed sharply higher, buoyed by subdued producer prices (PPI) data that lessened fears of an imminent rise in interest rates.

The FTSE 100 index closed at the day's best level, up 50.7 points at 4,107.3, and within reach of the December 31 high of 4,118.5. Gainers were in a three-to-one majority, with banks and insurance stocks leading the advance. Mid-250 stocks added 27.1 points to end at 4,534.9.
Government bonds, or gilts, supported stocks after the December's PPI report showed core factory gate prices up just 0.1 percent. The March long gilt future closed 18/32 higher at 109-17.

Interest rate concerns also looked set to keep the dollar firm. A rise of 262,000 in U.S. non-farm payrolls in December, reported on Friday, helped fire rate fever, while earnings data set inflation alarm bells ringing.

The firm dollar tone was helped by another assault on the mark on its European crosses. The spectacular rise of the Norwegian crown continued, pushing the mark below 4.00 crowns for the first time since September 1992.
"The dollar rally is all about interest rate rise speculation in the U.S. and rate cut expectations in Europe," said Ian Harwood, head of strategy and economics at Kleinwort Benson.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was trading at 116.38 yen and 1.6000 marks compared with 115.96 and 1.5855 late in Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index closed up 50.7 points, or 1.25 percent, at 4,107.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index closed up 33.77 points, or 1.45 percent, at a record 2,361.27.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 21.56 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,954.95. In late electronic trade, the IBIS DAX ended up 40.97 at 2.956.78.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $359.05, down five cents from Friday's London close. Silver ended down six cents at $4.71 after coming under selling pressure out of New York.
